title: Open Certificate Standard record, version 1
description: The shape of a certificate record. STRUCTURE ONLY. It deliberately permits null, empty strings and empty arrays, because under section 3 of the specification those are legal ways of saying a field was not answered, and they normalise away before hashing. A schema that demanded non-empty values would reject records that are perfectly valid. It also cannot express the canonicalisation rules, and passing it is not conformance: conformance is decided by the criteria in section 4, against a record whose hash has been checked.

spec.description: The version of the standard this record claims. A URI so it can be resolved.

dutyHolder.description: The landlord or managing agent, where the certificate is issued in respect of let premises.

issuer.description: The competent person who certified the work.

inspection.description: What was inspected, when, and under which certificate type.

date.description: The local calendar day the work was carried out, or empty if unanswered. Never re-zoned: see specification section 3, rule 8.

items.description: Per-item findings, in the order the engineer recorded them. Order is meaningful: appliance 1 is not appliance 2, and a blank entry keeps its place rather than being removed. An empty array means no items were recorded.

rules.description: The rules the certificate was made under, so it can be read years later against the edition it was issued against.

schemaId.description: Country-scoped, because type codes repeat across countries.

issuedAt.description: RFC 3339 instant in UTC at millisecond precision. See specification section 3, rule 9.

recordVersion.description: Revision of this record. 1 unless it has been reissued.

supersedes.description: Lowercase hex hash of the record this one replaces. A correction is a new record, never an edit.
